channel.title: Code Orange Dev School Articles
channel.description: Articles on Bitcoin self-custody, privacy, and open-source development from Code Orange Dev School.

item.title: Bitchat: Messaging Without the Internet, Tested at Our Workshops
item.description: We put Bitchat on everyone's phone at a Bitcoin House Bali meetup and messaged each other with no internet at all. Here is what Bitchat is, why it matters for censorship resistance, and what it felt like to try it.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: How to Defend Against a $5 Wrench Attack
item.description: Physical attacks on bitcoiners are rising, including in Bali. Here is the layered defence we teach at our self-custody workshops: good opsec, decoy wallets, passphrases, multisig and timelocks.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: How to Make Your First Contribution to Bitcoin Core
item.description: How to contribute to Bitcoin Core for the first time: build it, run the tests, review and test pull requests, and open your first small PR, step by step and in plain English.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Silent Payments Explained Simply: One Bitcoin Address, No Trail
item.description: Silent payments in Bitcoin, explained simply: how one reusable address can receive many payments that nobody can link together, what the catch is, and how to try it.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Why Bitcoin Needs Educators
item.description: Code on GitHub changes nothing until people know how to use it safely. Why teaching, writing guides and running study groups are real open-source contributions to Bitcoin.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Bitcoin in Bali: Where to Learn Bitcoin in Person
item.description: Looking for Bitcoin in Bali? Free monthly workshops, meetups and builder sessions at Bitcoin House Bali in Canggu, plus what you can learn there and how to join.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Free Bitcoin Courses You Can Start Today (2026 Guide)
item.description: The best free Bitcoin courses in 2026, from complete beginner to developer: what each one teaches, how long it takes, and how to actually finish one.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: How to Run a Bitcoin Node: A Beginner Guide (2026)
item.description: How to run a Bitcoin node in plain English: why it matters, what hardware you need, the four easiest setups (laptop, node box, Raspberry Pi, light node), and how to connect your wallet to it.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Multisig vs Hardware Wallet: Choosing Your Bitcoin Self-Custody Setup
item.description: Multisig vs hardware wallet: what each one protects you from, what can go wrong, and a simple step-by-step path to the right Bitcoin self-custody setup for you.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: What Is PayJoin? A Plain-English Guide (We Tested It Live)
item.description: What is PayJoin? A plain-English guide to the Bitcoin privacy trick that hides your payment amount, how PayJoin v2 works, which wallets support it, and what broke when we tested it live.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Why Our AI + Bitcoin Meetups Bring 3x More People
item.description: People come to our meetups to vibe code with AI and leave with a Lightning wallet, a node and an agent that can earn sats. Here is what we learned running AI + Bitcoin workshops in Bali and on Discord.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: We Tried to Mine a Bitcoin Block With a BitAxe
item.description: At our Bitcoin mining workshop we plugged in a BitAxe and agreed to split the 3.125 BTC reward if we found a block. Here is what a tiny home miner teaches you about proof of work, pools, energy and 51% attacks.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Privacy Isn't About Hiding. It's About Protection.
item.description: Bitcoin is pseudonymous, not anonymous. Here is how your balance, spending and IP address can leak, and the simple habits (fresh addresses, your own node, PayJoin, Silent Payments) that protect you.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: How to Become a Bitcoin Developer in 2026: A Free Roadmap
item.description: A free, step-by-step roadmap to becoming a Bitcoin developer in 2026: what to learn first, free courses, your first open-source contribution, and getting funded.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Just Show Up: Why Learning Bitcoin Together Works
item.description: Online on Discord or around a table at Bitcoin House Bali, learning Bitcoin with other people is faster and friendlier. Here is why to show up.
item.dc:creator: Andy

item.title: Why Self-Custody Matters: Get Your Bitcoin Off the Exchange
item.description: Why leaving bitcoin on an exchange means holding an IOU, and three simple steps to start self-custody with a hardware wallet and a tested seed phrase backup.
item.dc:creator: Andy
